overview.title: Student & Teacher Overview: Lesson 20
overview.text: In this lesson, you will connect algebraic equations in two variables to geometric curves. A solution to an equation with two variables is an ordered pair $(x, y)$ that produces a true numerical statement. The graph of the equation is the visual plotting of its infinite solution set.
outcomes: Recognize and identify ordered pair solutions $(x, y)$ to two-variable linear equations $Ax + By = C$.
Understand that the graph of a line is a visual representation of all infinite solutions to the equation.
Verify whether any given point $(x_0, y_0)$ lies on the line by testing if it satisfies the equation.
overview.teacherInsight: Stress that a line on a coordinate plane is not just a geometric line segment: it is literally a cloud of infinite points packed together, each of which is an exact solution $(x,y)$ to the equation.

vocabulary.definition: A pair of numbers (x, y) written in a specific order representing a unique point on a coordinate plane.
The set of all points on the coordinate plane whose coordinates (x, y) satisfy the equation.

practiceQuestions.question: Which of the following points lies on the graph of $3x - 2y = 12$?
practiceQuestions.explanation: Test $(4, 0)$: $3(4) - 2(0) = 12 - 0 = 12$. Since $12 = 12$, $(4, 0)$ is a solution and lies on the graph.

practiceQuestions.question: How many ordered pair solutions exist for the equation $y = 3x - 5$?
practiceQuestions.explanation: For every real number chosen for $x$, there is a corresponding real number $y$. Thus, there are infinitely many points along the continuous line.
